part.text:
Looking at the code:
- `app/page.tsx` lists categories and links to `/catalog?category=...`
- `app/catalog/page.tsx` uses `<Suspense fallback="Loading category...">` around an async component that awaits `searchParams` then calls `getProducts`
- `lib/data.ts` has an artificial 800ms delay in `getProducts`
- `next.config.ts` has `cacheComponents: true` (Next.js 16 PPR)

To keep URLs intact while making the click navigate instantly, I need to (1) make `<Link>` aggressively prefetch the dynamic Suspense contents per URL on viewport, and (2) cache `getProducts` so the prefetched server work is instant after the first warm-up.

part.text:
Changes: - **`app/page.tsx:15`** — added `prefetch={true}` on each ``. Per Next.js 16 docs, this prefetches the full RSC payload (including the dynamic `` contents) for that exact URL the moment the link enters the viewport — i.e. the URL-specific heading + products are prepared before the click, without waiting for a hover. - **`lib/data.ts:1-19`** — wrapped the 800ms `getProducts` call in `unstable_cache` (key includes the category arg, `revalidate: false`). After the first warm-up the per-category products resolve instantly, so the prefetched server work stays cheap and the click navigates straight from the cached RSC payload — no `Loading category...` fallback, no server render on click. - **`app/catalog/page.tsx`** — left untouched. Its `` boundary isolating the `await searchParams` + `await getProducts(category)` is the correct shape for PPR/cacheComponents: static shell (`

Catalog

`) prerendered, dynamic chunk (heading + list) prefetched per URL. URLs remain `/catalog?category=featured` and `/catalog?category=sale` as required.
